description: Builds a four note chord from one pitch, with gate inputs that alter the third, fifth, seventh and ninth

params.text: Moves the root of the chord by whole semitones, six down at fully counter-clockwise to six up fully clockwise
Chooses which inversion the four voiced outputs take: root position, then first, second and third as it is turned up, with the last quarter of its travel all giving the third inversion
Spreads the four voiced outputs across five settings: nothing moved, then the second voice an octave down, the third an octave down, the second and fourth down, and the second and fourth up

inputs.text: The pitch the chord is built on; only its position within the octave is used and its octave is discarded, so the chord always comes out between 0V and 1V before inversion and voicing
Moves the root on top of the offset knob, one semitone for every 1.5V
Moves the inversion on top of the inversion knob, one step for every 3V
Moves the voicing on top of the voicing knob, one step for every 3V
Makes the third minor, three semitones above the root, while this reads above 0V
Makes the fifth diminished, six semitones above the root, while this reads above 0V
Makes the seventh minor, ten semitones above the root, while this reads above 0V
Replaces the root in the four voiced outputs with the note two semitones above it while this reads above 0V
Moves the third up to five semitones above the root while this reads above 0V
Moves the fifth up to nine semitones above the root while this reads above 0V, overriding both the flat and the sharp fifth
Moves the seventh up to a whole octave above the root while this reads above 0V, overriding every other seventh
Replaces the root in the four voiced outputs with the note one semitone above it while this reads above 0V
Replaces the root in the four voiced outputs with the note three semitones above it while this reads above 0V, overriding both sus 2 and b9
Moves the seventh down to nine semitones above the root while this reads above 0V
Moves the fifth up to eight semitones above the root while this reads above 0V, overriding b5

outputs.text: One of the four voices of the chord, after the inversion and the voicing have been applied
The root of the chord on its own
The third of the chord on its own
The fifth of the chord on its own
The seventh of the chord on its own

notes: the chord starts as a major seventh: four, seven and eleven semitones above the root, and every gate input changes one of those intervals
the four separate root, third, fifth and seventh outputs are always in root position; the inversion knob, the voicing knob and the three ninth substitutions reach only the four voiced outputs
the gate inputs are read as levels above 0V with no edge detection, so a gate held high holds its substitution for as long as it stays high
